subject: A simple question, Minister: have farmers been targeted?
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

I am writing to ask you to state one thing plainly, in writing.

Confirm that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Greg Baldwin.

Mr Baldwin rang triple zero to report trespassers on his own farm. He was the one charged. On 27 April 2026 the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every single charge against him. There was never a case to answer.

A farmer was put through that. Victorians are entitled to know whether it was the result of any direction, encouragement or pressure involving your office or your department.

If the answer is no, say so. A denial takes one sentence and you have not yet given it. Every day that passes without one, people draw their own conclusions.

I would appreciate a direct written response.

Yours sincerely,

subject: The DPP withdrew every charge. Now answer the question.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

On 27 April 2026 the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every charge against farmer Greg Baldwin. Not some of them. All of them.

That is not a technicality. It means a Victorian farmer was dragged through the courts over a matter that should never have reached them.

So I am asking you to confirm, on the record, that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Mr Baldwin.

I am not asking for a media statement about the energy transition. I am asking for a direct answer to a direct question, in writing, from the Minister responsible.

If no one in your department had any hand in what happened to Mr Baldwin, that should be simple to say. Please say it.

Yours sincerely,

subject: He called triple zero. He got charged. Explain that, Minister.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

Greg Baldwin found people on his farm he had not authorised to be there. He did exactly what any of us would tell our kids to do: he rang triple zero.

The farmer was the one who ended up charged. On 27 April 2026 the DPP withdrew every charge against him.

Minister, I want to hear it from you directly: confirm that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Greg Baldwin.

Every farming family in this state is now asking whether calling the police to their own front gate will land them in court. You can put that to rest with one clear sentence. Refusing to give it tells us something too.

I look forward to your written reply.

Yours sincerely,

subject: $6,000 threats on their own land — was that sanctioned?
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

The Baldwin family were threatened with $6,000 fines on their own property by contractors seeking access.

I am asking you to confirm in writing that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Greg Baldwin, and that no contractor acting on your department's behalf was ever authorised to threaten a landholder that way.

Remember that when this reached a courtroom, the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every charge against Mr Baldwin on 27 April 2026.

Farmers are entitled to know exactly what instructions are being handed to the people turning up at their gates, and who signed off on them. Please release that detail, and please answer the question directly.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Put it in writing, Minister
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

I am a Victorian and I am asking you for something very ordinary: an answer.

Confirm that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Greg Baldwin.

The facts that prompt the question are on the public record. Mr Baldwin reported trespassers on his own farm by calling triple zero, was charged himself, and on 27 April 2026 the DPP withdrew every charge against him.

Ministers are accountable to the people who pay for their departments. I am not asking you to comment on a court matter or to speculate about anyone else. I am asking you to state your own department's conduct, plainly, in writing.

I would like a response I can read for myself, not a press release.

Yours sincerely,

subject: One sentence would settle this
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

This email asks for one sentence from you.

"Neither I nor my department has ever targeted farmers, including Greg Baldwin."

If that sentence is true, writing it costs you nothing and would reassure thousands of farming families across this state. If you will not write it, people are entitled to ask why.

The background is not in dispute. Mr Baldwin called triple zero about trespassers on his own farm, was charged himself, and on 27 April 2026 the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every charge.

I am asking you, as the Minister responsible, to give that sentence in writing.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Soldier-settlement land, three generations, one question
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

Some of the properties your department is seeking access to have been in the same families for generations, including land granted to soldiers who came home and were told it was theirs.

Greg Baldwin rang triple zero about trespassers on his farm. He was charged. On 27 April 2026 the DPP withdrew every charge against him.

I am asking you to confirm plainly that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Mr Baldwin.

These families are not obstacles to be managed. They are Victorians who have done everything asked of them for decades. They deserve a straight answer from the Minister rather than silence.

Please reply in writing.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Your silence is becoming the answer, Minister
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

The question has now been put to you many times and you have not answered it.

Confirm that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Greg Baldwin.

Mr Baldwin called triple zero to report trespassers on his own farm and was charged himself. On 27 April 2026 the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every charge. There was no case.

I understand that ministers receive a great deal of correspondence. This one is short and it asks for a yes or a no. Continuing to say nothing is itself a message, and it is being heard clearly across regional Victoria.

I would welcome a direct written answer.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Farmers are now afraid to call the police. That's on you to fix.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

Something has broken in rural Victoria. Farmers are telling each other not to ring the police if they find strangers on their land, because of what happened to Greg Baldwin.

He made that call. He was charged. On 27 April 2026 the DPP withdrew every charge against him.

Minister, I am asking you to confirm in writing that neither you nor your department has ever targeted farmers, including Mr Baldwin.

When people stop trusting that the law protects them on their own property, that is a serious problem, and it is one you are in a position to address today with a clear public statement.

Please provide one.

Yours sincerely,

subject: On the record please, Minister: were farmers ever targeted?
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

I am writing to request a written, on-the-record answer to a single question.

Has your department, or you as Minister, ever targeted farmers, including Greg Baldwin? I am asking you to confirm that the answer is no.

The reason for the question is a matter of record: Mr Baldwin rang triple zero over trespassers on his own farm, was charged, and on 27 April 2026 the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every charge against him.

Alongside that confirmation, I would ask you to disclose the instructions and scripts issued to contractors approaching Victorian farms, so landholders know exactly what they are dealing with.

Thank you for your time. I will be looking out for your reply.

Yours sincerely,
